title: Settlement of Vending Services Program Statements and the Late Charge
content:
Vending Services Program statements fall due the number of days after the statement date printed against the programme, and a payment is recorded against the single statement it settles. A payment is accepted while the agreement stands active, suspended or closed, since a collected estate may still carry a final statement; the standing of the agreement and the balance outstanding on it are read from the vending agreement record before the payment is posted.

A part payment settles the named statement in part and never spills onto another; an overpayment leaves the excess on the agreement to be applied to the next statement raised.

A late charge is the monthly late percentage printed against the programme applied to the amount still outstanding once the grace days printed against the same programme have passed, held to the late charge ceiling printed against that programme.

Where a statement is disputed in writing before the grace days expire, no late charge is raised while the dispute stands open, and commission due to the client is still paid out.

Once a statement is past due by the credit hold threshold printed against the programme, restocking stops and the machines are drawn down to empty, until the balance is settled.

### Where a payment lands

| The payment received | Where it lands |
| --- | --- |
| Less than the named statement | against that statement, settling it in part; the remainder of that statement stands outstanding |
| Equal to the named statement | against that statement, settling it |
| More than the named statement | against that statement, with the excess left on the agreement for the next statement raised |

A payment is never spread across two statements of its own accord: it is recorded against the one statement it settles, and a part payment leaves the rest of that statement outstanding rather than reaching another.

### The late charge worked through (hypothetical amounts)

The base of the late charge is the amount still outstanding once the grace days have passed, not the amount the statement was raised at. Where a statement of 1200.00 has been met in part by a payment of 400.00 before the grace days pass, the base is 800.00, and a monthly late percentage of 2.00 percent gives a charge of 16.00 for the month, which stands below a ceiling of 300.00 and is raised in full. Where the same percentage on a larger outstanding amount would give 450.00, the charge raised against that vending invoice is 300.00, since the charge is held to the ceiling printed against the programme. The amounts and the percentage chosen here are illustrative and are not programme figures.

### The late charge, the dispute and the credit hold

A late charge is raised once the grace days printed against the programme have passed, on the amount then still outstanding. Where a statement is disputed in writing before those grace days expire, no late charge is raised for as long as the dispute stands open, and the client's commission continues to be paid out through it. The credit hold threshold is a further and separate point, counted in days past due: once a statement has been past due by that number of days, restocking on the agreement stops and the machines are drawn down to empty, and that holds until the balance is settled.
